items.project_definition: The most permissive type assigned when a specific data structure is not yet defined within the static analysis of the source code.
The set of endpoints providing structured data exchange between the client and the server via defined routes.
Attributes used to enhance the accessibility of web elements for assistive technologies.
The server-side logic handler responsible for verifying user credentials and generating security tokens.
A security mechanism that allows or restricts requested resources on a web page to be requested from another domain.
A synchronization milestone indicating that a specific set of prerequisites is fully operational before advancing to the next phase.
The interface element enabling the user to toggle the tracking status of a specific sporting event.
The backend logic layer managing the creation and removal of tracking associations between users and events.
The view component that renders a filtered list of events designated as interesting by the authenticated user.
The primary functional objective that a specific user story must satisfy to be considered successful.
A unique alphanumeric identifier used to target a specific database record for retrieval or modification.
The phased deployment approach where the system is built in successive operational layers from foundation to polish.
The lightweight data-interchange format used for all server-client communication payloads.
The compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties for authentication.
The minimum set of features required to provide a working version of the system to users.
The specific boundary of deliverables comprising the first three operational phases.
A reusable UI element representing a summarized view of a single sporting event.
The interface component displaying comprehensive data, including venue and team crests, for a specific event.
The layout component responsible for iterating and rendering a collection of event summaries.
The backend logic provider for retrieving, filtering, and processing event-related data.
Functions that execute during the request-response cycle to perform cross-cutting concerns like logging or authentication.
The structural grouping of development tasks based on user stories to facilitate independent testing.
The set of required design and specification documents that must be available before implementation begins.
The root-level documentation file containing environment setup and system usage instructions.
The frontend library used for building the user interface via a component-based architecture.
Optional validation suites including unit and integration checks to ensure code reliability.
The strongly typed superset of JavaScript used across both client and server layers.
The visual layer and interaction elements the end-user utilizes to navigate the application.
The relational entity mapping the association between a registered account and a specific sporting event.
The combined software system consisting of the backend server and the frontend client.
A priority marker indicating that a phase is a hard blocking dependency for all subsequent user story work.
